 3m ago 14.26 EST Full-time: Nottingham Forest 3-1 Manchester City
 Having won their first seven, City have now lost three in a row, but this was all about Forest. They had the right gameplan for City and executed it perfectly. Delap was excellent and Glasner’s words to fire up his side in the week clearly worked.
 Share 5m ago 14.25 EST 90+4 min Late yellow for Netz for bringing down Foden.
 Share Updated at  14.26 EST 6m ago 14.23 EST 90+2 min Roars from Igor Jesus as he gets the better of Khusanov near the byline and wins a pressure-easing goal kick.
 Share Updated at  14.24 EST 9m ago 14.21 EST 90+1 min We’re into four added minutes.
 Share Updated at  14.21 EST 9m ago 14.20 EST 89 min Forest are still scrapping away, Gibbs-White gives away a free-kick deep in City’s half but that’ll help the second tick away. Very impressive performance from Forest.
 Share Updated at  14.21 EST 12m ago 14.18 EST 86 min There are some City fans in the away end who have their replica shirts with ‘Cheetos’ as the main sponsor. That is great needle but does make it hard to have any sympathy. Off goes Delap to a standing ovation, no hat-trick for him. Igor Jesus is on to make his comeback from a calf injury.
 Share Updated at  14.21 EST 15m ago 14.15 EST 84 min Big Vange is looking happy in the director’s box.
 Share Updated at  14.21 EST 16m ago 14.14 EST 82 min Delap wins a free-kick high up the pitch as he outscraps Nunes. That’s great centre-forward play. Time is getting away from City now.
 Share Updated at  14.21 EST 18m ago 14.12 EST 80 min Gibbs-White has been exactly what Forest need today. Nuggety and aggressive in the press, quality on the ball. His latest touch is a backheel nutmeg that befuddles Nunes.
 Share Updated at  14.12 EST 20m ago 14.09 EST 78 min Fernández goes off to be replaced by Phil Foden, round of boos for Argentinian. Sometimes hard to believe that Fernández has been sold for fees of more than £200m. He was awful today.
 Share Updated at  14.12 EST 22m ago 14.07 EST 76 min O’Reilly wins a corner, poor ball from Fernández and Sels claims.
 Share Updated at  14.12 EST 23m ago 14.07 EST 75 min Glasner sprints off down the touchline to celebrate with his players. Without wanting to get all celebration police, that’s a bit much from a manager for a league game in November.
 Share 24m ago 14.05 EST Goal! Nottingham Forest 3-1 Manchester City (Delap 73)
 This is almost a carbon copy of his goal from the first half, Forest turnover, direct running at the City defence, this time from Gibbs-White, before Delap powers it into the top corner, with his left foot this time. Some finish.
 View image in fullscreen Liam Delap scores a cracker! Photograph: Chris Radburn/Reuters View image in fullscreen That was some finish from Delap. Photograph: Chris Radburn/Reuters Share Updated at  14.20 EST 29m ago 14.01 EST 69 min Murillo wins the ball off Fernández again and this time goes for goal from inside his own half. Woeful. That’s closer to the corner flag.
 Share Updated at  14.12 EST 30m ago 13.59 EST 66 min Anderson has been excellent, Enzo Fernández less so. The Argentinian loses the ball to Murillo on the edge of his own box and the turnover allows Yates to get a shot off, it’s deflcted and clip the top of the bar. City eventually clear the corner and Ndiaye leads a quick counter that is halted by a the recently introduced Ndoye. Yellow card for what was almost a rugby tackle.
 Share Updated at  14.13 EST 34m ago 13.56 EST 64 min Muñoz and McAtee are withdrawn, on come Ndoye and Netz for Forest.
 Share Updated at  14.13 EST 34m ago 13.55 EST 63 min Forest fans and players are incensed as Delap is denied a free-kick when Khusanov bundles him over. VAR has a quick check on the follow-up challenge from McAtee as the Forest man piles into Anderson, yellow card.
 Share Updated at  14.13 EST 38m ago 13.52 EST 59 min You have to say the changes have worked for City. O’Reilly shows nice feet in the box after linking up with Doku and it’s deflected away for a corner. Doku has been freed up and Nunes simply carries more threat down the right. A selection error from Maresca in hindsight.
 Share Updated at  14.13 EST 40m ago 13.49 EST 57 min Chance for Haaland and that is an uncharacteristic miss. The City forward has a bit of space in the box to get a short off but his scoopy side-foot goes over.
 Share Updated at  14.13 EST 42m ago 13.48 EST 55 min Gibbs-White is hobbling a little after a crunching tackle from Nunes. The Forest talisman was sold a little short by Nico Williams’ pass and the City man left a bit on him. Not nasty, just firm.
 Share Updated at  14.13 EST 45m ago 13.45 EST 54 min Did that hit the post? Doku spins away from his man tries to sweep it across the Haaland, the ball takes a deflection and almost wrongfoots Sels. The Forest keeper does well to gather the resulting corner at the second attempt.
 Share Updated at  14.13 EST 46m ago 13.43 EST Goal! Nottingham Forest 2-1 Manchester City (Cherki 52)
 And that is why he was kept on! Sweet, sweet hit first time on the half-volley from Cherki as the ball fell to him on the edge of the box. Game on.
 View image in fullscreen Cherki leathers in a response for City! Photograph: Andrew Boyers/Action Images/Reuters Share Updated at  13.50 EST 50m ago 13.40 EST 49 min Jeers as Cherki misplaces a pass straight of play. I’d say he was lucky to survive the half-time cull.
 Share Updated at  14.13 EST 51m ago 13.39 EST 48 min Khusanov has come into the centre of the City backline and has to stretch his legs up against Delap. The Uzbek is quick and wins a free-kick as Delap barges into the back of him.
 Share Updated at  13.39 EST 53m ago 13.37 EST Peeeeeep!
 We’re back under way and City have made changes. Nico O’Reilly has replaced Gvardiol and Guéhi is hauled off so Matheus Nunes can enter the fray.
 Share Updated at  13.39 EST 55m ago 13.35 EST We have roundups too! Here’s the best of the WSL action , the Championship in brief and coverage from across Europe .
 Share 1h ago 13.31 EST Aaron Bower Okafor’s winner for Leeds adds insult to Tel’s injury for Spurs as Bogle escapes red 
 It is almost one year to the day when the Leeds manager, Daniel Farke, produced the tactical overhaul many observers believe saved his job. That day, Farke abandoned his trusted 4-3-3 when Leeds were 2-0 down at Manchester City and although they lost the game, the 3-5-2 he reverted to was the bedrock for the success that followed.
 Read Aaron Bower’s full report from Elland Road: 
 Okafor’s Leeds winner adds insult to Tel’s injury for Tottenham as Bogle escapes red Read more View image in fullscreen Mathys Tel receives medical attention after a tackle by Jayden Bogle which the VAR took several minutes to clear. Photograph: Scott Heppell/Reuters Share 1h ago 13.28 EST Jacob Steinberg Muniz rescues late point for Fulham against Newcastle after Murphy stunner 
 Rodrigo Muniz came off the bench to rescue a point for Fulham and deny Matthias Jaissle a welcome victory after a difficult week. Newcastle produced an improved display after a run of four defeats in five games in all competitions but they could not hold out after going 1-0 up thanks to a vicious late strike from Jacob Murphy.
 Jacob Steinberg’s full report from Craven Cottage: 
 Muniz rescues late point for Fulham against Newcastle after Murphy stunner Read more View image in fullscreen Rodrigo Muniz turns in Fulham’s equaliser in the 83rd minute. Photograph: Dylan Martinez/Reuters Share 1h ago 13.25 EST Ed Aarons Ødegaard extends Arsenal lead at top with winner to break Hull resistance 
 As most Arsenal supporters would testify, patience is a virtue. They needed plenty during the 22-year wait to be crowned Premier League champions and Mikel Arteta’s side certainly had to retain their composure as they tried to break down a dogged Hull team. They had not beaten Arsenal in 14 attempts since winning on their first visit to this ground in 2008. But with 20 minutes still to play, there was every chance that Sergej Jakirovic’s team could have pulled off one of the shocks of the season.

 Share 1h ago 13.21 EST Half-time: Nottingham Forest 2-0 Manchester City
 That’s the first half up, great 45 minutes of football, especially if you’re of the Forest persuasion.
